paragraphs.title: Remembering the Way and Keeping the Commandments

easy.question: What does Moses command the people to do?
answers: Keep and obey all the commandments
Build cities in the wilderness
Gather the manna
easy.explanation: The verse says, “All the commandments... shall ye observe to do.”

easy.question: How many years did the Lord lead Israel through the wilderness?
answers: Ten years
Forty years
Seventy years
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord led Israel through the wilderness for forty years.

easy.question: What did not happen to the Israelites during the forty years in the wilderness?
answers: They did not eat food
They did not hear commandments
Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell
easy.explanation: The passage says that their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.

medium.question: Why did the Lord lead Israel through the wilderness, according to these verses?
answers: To humble and test them, and see whether they would keep His commandments
To keep them away from every land
To teach them how to build houses
medium.explanation: The wilderness experience humbled and tested the people to reveal whether they would keep the Lord’s commandments.

medium.question: What did the Lord want to teach Israel through the manna?
answers: That people should eat only in the wilderness
That man does not live by bread only, but by every word from the Lord
That manna is better than every other food
medium.explanation: The manna taught that life depends not only on food, but also on every word that comes from the Lord.

medium.question: In the phrase “to humble thee, and to prove thee,” what does “to prove thee” mean?
answers: To give you a gift
To lead you into the land
To test you
medium.explanation: Here, “to prove thee” means to test you and reveal whether you would keep the commandments.

challenge.question: What does the comparison “as a man chasteneth his son” teach about the Lord’s relationship with Israel?
answers: The Lord disciplines and corrects Israel as a father disciplines his son
The Lord wants to punish Israel without reason
The Lord treats Israel as enemies
challenge.explanation: The comparison presents discipline as part of a father’s instruction and care.

challenge.question: What idea connects the hunger, the manna, and the statement about every word from the Lord?
answers: Hunger proved that people must not eat in the wilderness
The manna taught that human survival depends also on the Lord’s will and word
The manna was meant to replace all the commandments
challenge.explanation: The Lord allowed Israel to hunger and then gave them manna to teach that people do not live by bread alone.

challenge.question: What main sequence emerges from these verses about the purpose of the wilderness journey?
answers: To remain in the wilderness, eat manna, and reject the commandments
To reach the land immediately without being tested
To be tested, learn dependence on the Lord, and keep His commandments
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the wilderness years, testing, manna, and the command to keep the Lord’s ways.

questions.question: What does the comparison “as a man chasteneth his son” teach about the Lord’s relationship with Israel?
answers: The Lord disciplines and corrects Israel as a father disciplines his son
The Lord wants to punish Israel without reason
The Lord treats Israel as enemies
questions.explanation: The comparison presents discipline as part of a father’s instruction and care.

questions.question: What idea connects the hunger, the manna, and the statement about every word from the Lord?
answers: Hunger proved that people must not eat in the wilderness
The manna taught that human survival depends also on the Lord’s will and word
The manna was meant to replace all the commandments
questions.explanation: The Lord allowed Israel to hunger and then gave them manna to teach that people do not live by bread alone.

questions.question: What main sequence emerges from these verses about the purpose of the wilderness journey?
answers: To remain in the wilderness, eat manna, and reject the commandments
To reach the land immediately without being tested
To be tested, learn dependence on the Lord, and keep His commandments
questions.explanation: The verses connect the wilderness years, testing, manna, and the command to keep the Lord’s ways.

paragraphs.title: The Good Land and Its Abundant Blessings

easy.question: How is the land described that the Lord is bringing Israel into?
answers: A good land
A small land
A distant land
easy.explanation: The passage explicitly calls it “a good land.”

easy.question: What sources of water are mentioned in the land?
answers: Rivers and seas
Brooks, fountains, and depths
Rain and snow
easy.explanation: The passage mentions brooks of water, fountains, and depths.

easy.question: What should the Israelites do after they have eaten and are full?
answers: Build houses
Go to war
Bless the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says, “When thou hast eaten and art full, then thou shalt bless the Lord.”

medium.question: What is the connection between the land’s abundance and the command to bless the Lord?
answers: The abundance proves that the Lord is unnecessary
The abundance is a gift from the Lord, so they should thank Him
The abundance was given only to the leaders
medium.explanation: The good land and its abundance come from the Lord, so the people should bless Him.

medium.question: What order of events appears in verse 10?
answers: They bless, eat, and then become full
They become full, bless, and then eat
They eat, become full, and then bless the Lord
medium.explanation: The verse gives the order: “thou shalt eat... and art full, then thou shalt bless.”

medium.question: What does the phrase “without scarceness” mean in the description of the land?
answers: Without poverty or lack
With joy and dancing
Quickly and hurriedly
medium.explanation: The context says that nothing will be lacking in the land, so “without scarceness” means without poverty or shortage.

challenge.question: What combination of resources is described in the land?
answers: Only water and pasture
Food, water, and metals
Only trees and stones
challenge.explanation: The verses mention water sources, crops, iron, and brass.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the fact that the fountains and depths spring out of valleys and hills?
answers: Water is found in only one region
The hills are unsuitable for settlement
Water sources are found in different areas of the land
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both valleys and hills shows that the water sources are not limited to one geographic area.

challenge.question: Why does the mention of stones, iron, and brass strengthen the idea that the land lacks nothing?
answers: Because it contains raw materials for building and making tools
Because the metals are used as food
Because the stones create the fountains
challenge.explanation: Iron and brass are natural resources that can be taken from the land and used for construction and tools.

questions.question: What combination of resources is described in the land?
answers: Only water and pasture
Food, water, and metals
Only trees and stones
questions.explanation: The verses mention water sources, crops, iron, and brass.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that the fountains and depths spring out of valleys and hills?
answers: Water is found in only one region
The hills are unsuitable for settlement
Water sources are found in different areas of the land
questions.explanation: Mentioning both valleys and hills shows that the water sources are not limited to one geographic area.

questions.question: Why does the mention of stones, iron, and brass strengthen the idea that the land lacks nothing?
answers: Because it contains raw materials for building and making tools
Because the metals are used as food
Because the stones create the fountains
questions.explanation: Iron and brass are natural resources that can be taken from the land and used for construction and tools.

paragraphs.title: The Danger of Abundance and Forgetting the Lord

easy.question: What does Moses warn the people not to do?
answers: Forget the Lord
Leave the land
Eat bread
easy.explanation: Moses warns the people not to forget the Lord or stop keeping His commandments.

easy.question: What things are described as increasing among the people?
answers: Only houses
Herds, flocks, silver, and gold
Only food
easy.explanation: The verses describe the increase of herds, flocks, silver, gold, and possessions.

easy.question: What may happen when a person’s heart is lifted up?
answers: He will build a house
He will increase his flocks
He will forget the Lord
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord.”

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: Abundance and possessions, pride, and then forgetting the Lord
Forgetting the Lord, poverty, and then building houses
Leaving Egypt, poverty, and then leaving the land
medium.explanation: The verses first describe eating, prosperity, and possessions; then pride; and finally forgetting the Lord.

medium.question: In the phrase “Then thine heart be lifted up,” what does “lifted up” mean?
answers: Become tired
Become proud
Become hungry
medium.explanation: In this context, a lifted-up heart means becoming proud.

medium.question: Why can abundance and possessions be dangerous according to this passage?
answers: They make a person leave his home
They prevent a person from eating
They may cause a person to become proud and forget the Lord
medium.explanation: Abundance itself is not forbidden, but it can lead to pride and forgetting the Lord.

challenge.question: Why does the verse mention that the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt, “from the house of bondage”?
answers: To remind them that the Lord saved them and gave them freedom
To explain how they built fine houses
To describe the increase of their herds and flocks
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the Exodus reminds the people of the Lord’s mercy and that their freedom and prosperity are not solely their own achievement.

challenge.question: What is the main connection between verse 11 and verses 12–14?
answers: Verse 11 discusses war, while the other verses discuss peace
Verse 11 warns against forgetting the Lord, and the following verses describe what may cause it
Verse 11 commands them to build houses, and the following verses cancel that command
challenge.explanation: Verse 11 gives the warning, while verses 12–14 describe how prosperity, houses, and possessions may lead to forgetting the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the precise emphasis of the warning in this passage?
answers: It is forbidden to eat or build houses
It is forbidden to have silver or gold
The Lord must not be forgotten precisely when a person enjoys prosperity and success
challenge.explanation: The verses do not forbid food, houses, or possessions; they warn that prosperity may cause people to forget its source.

questions.question: Why does the verse mention that the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt, “from the house of bondage”?
answers: To remind them that the Lord saved them and gave them freedom
To explain how they built fine houses
To describe the increase of their herds and flocks
questions.explanation: Mentioning the Exodus reminds the people of the Lord’s mercy and that their freedom and prosperity are not solely their own achievement.

questions.question: What is the main connection between verse 11 and verses 12–14?
answers: Verse 11 discusses war, while the other verses discuss peace
Verse 11 warns against forgetting the Lord, and the following verses describe what may cause it
Verse 11 commands them to build houses, and the following verses cancel that command
questions.explanation: Verse 11 gives the warning, while verses 12–14 describe how prosperity, houses, and possessions may lead to forgetting the Lord.

questions.question: What is the precise emphasis of the warning in this passage?
answers: It is forbidden to eat or build houses
It is forbidden to have silver or gold
The Lord must not be forgotten precisely when a person enjoys prosperity and success
questions.explanation: The verses do not forbid food, houses, or possessions; they warn that prosperity may cause people to forget its source.

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Care in the Wilderness and the Source of Strength

easy.question: What dangers in the wilderness are described?
answers: Fiery serpents, scorpions, and thirst
Floods, snow, and winds
Lions, bears, and rain
easy.explanation: The passage mentions fiery serpents, scorpions, drought, and the absence of water.

easy.question: What did the Lord give the Israelites to eat in the wilderness?
answers: Bread from the ground
Manna
Fruit
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord fed them with manna in the wilderness.

easy.question: What should the Israelites remember when they have strength and wealth?
answers: That they are strong by themselves
That the wilderness was easy for them
That the Lord gives them power to get wealth
easy.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the Lord gives the power to achieve success and wealth.

medium.question: Why did the Lord give the Israelites manna, according to the passage?
answers: To humble and test them, and ultimately do them good
To teach them how to grow crops
So they would not need to enter the land
medium.explanation: The verse says that the manna was given to humble and test the people and to do them good in the end.

medium.question: In the phrase “to do thee good at thy latter end,” what does “at thy latter end” mean?
answers: Only in the last place
In the future or at the end of the process
Behind your back
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the future outcome or the end of the journey.

medium.question: What connection do these verses show between human success and remembering the Lord?
answers: Success proves that people do not need the Lord
Remembering the Lord matters only in the wilderness
People must remember that the Lord gave them the power to succeed
medium.explanation: The verses warn people not to credit their success only to their own strength, but to remember that the Lord gives them power.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “water out of the rock of flint” emphasize?
answers: That the Lord supplied water from a hard and unexpected place
That the water came from an ordinary stream
That the people dug a well in soft ground
challenge.explanation: Flint is hard rock, so the phrase emphasizes the miracle and the Lord’s ability to provide water in the wilderness.

challenge.question: Why does the passage say that the manna was unknown to their fathers?
answers: To teach that their fathers ate only meat
To emphasize that the Lord provided new and special food
To prove that manna was ordinary food
challenge.explanation: Saying that their fathers did not know the manna emphasizes that it was special food provided by the Lord.

challenge.question: How does verse 18 connect Israel’s success with the covenant with the fathers?
answers: Success cancels the covenant
The covenant depends only on Israel’s strength
The Lord gives power to succeed in order to establish the covenant He swore to the fathers
challenge.explanation: The verse teaches that Israel’s strength and success are connected to the Lord’s keeping of His covenant promise.

questions.question: What does the phrase “water out of the rock of flint” emphasize?
answers: That the Lord supplied water from a hard and unexpected place
That the water came from an ordinary stream
That the people dug a well in soft ground
questions.explanation: Flint is hard rock, so the phrase emphasizes the miracle and the Lord’s ability to provide water in the wilderness.

answers: To teach that their fathers ate only meat
To emphasize that the Lord provided new and special food
To prove that manna was ordinary food
questions.explanation: Saying that their fathers did not know the manna emphasizes that it was special food provided by the Lord.

questions.question: How does verse 18 connect Israel’s success with the covenant with the fathers?
answers: Success cancels the covenant
The covenant depends only on Israel’s strength
The Lord gives power to succeed in order to establish the covenant He swore to the fathers
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that Israel’s strength and success are connected to the Lord’s keeping of His covenant promise.

easy.question: Whom does the passage warn Israel not to follow?
answers: Other gods
The priests
The people of the land
easy.explanation: The passage warns, “walk after other gods, and serve them, and worship them.”

easy.question: What will happen to those who forget the Lord and serve other gods?
answers: They will gain wealth
They will perish
They will return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says, “ye shall surely perish.”

easy.question: Whom does the Lord destroy according to the passage?
answers: The priests
The Israelites
The nations before whom Israel enters the land
easy.explanation: The passage compares Israel’s possible destruction to that of the nations the Lord destroys before them.

medium.question: What sequence of actions is described in the passage?
answers: Forgetting the Lord, following other gods, and serving and worshiping them
Serving the Lord, forgetting Him, and then going to war
Entering the land, building a temple, and then forgetting the law
medium.explanation: The passage describes forgetting the Lord, following other gods, and then serving and worshiping them.

medium.question: In the phrase “because ye would not be obedient unto the voice of the Lord,” what does “because” indicate?
answers: What happened before
The reason for the punishment
A nearby location
medium.explanation: The phrase gives the reason Israel would perish: they would not obey the Lord’s voice.

medium.question: What is the relationship between disobeying the Lord and Israel’s destruction?
answers: Disobedience is the reason for the destruction
Disobedience prevents the destruction
The passage gives no connection between them
medium.explanation: The passage directly connects Israel’s destruction with refusing to obey the Lord.

challenge.question: Why does the passage say “ye shall surely perish” rather than simply “ye shall perish”?
answers: To emphasize that the destruction would be certain or complete
To say that the destruction would last only one day
To describe stronger remembrance
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes the certainty and seriousness of the destruction.

challenge.question: What does the comparison with “the nations which the Lord destroyeth before your face” teach about Israel?
answers: Israel can never be punished
Israel may also be punished if they act like the nations
The nations are stronger than Israel
challenge.explanation: The comparison teaches that punishment for disobedience and idolatry can also come upon Israel.

challenge.question: What is the central condition leading to the punishment described in these verses?
answers: Refusing to obey the Lord and following other gods
Lack of food in the wilderness
Conflict between the tribes of Israel
challenge.explanation: The verses connect destruction with forgetting the Lord, serving other gods, and refusing to obey His voice.

questions.question: Why does the passage say “ye shall surely perish” rather than simply “ye shall perish”?
answers: To emphasize that the destruction would be certain or complete
To say that the destruction would last only one day
To describe stronger remembrance
questions.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes the certainty and seriousness of the destruction.
